response.sql: WITH fielders AS (SELECT p.bats, COUNT(DISTINCT f.player_id) AS cnt FROM fielding f JOIN player p ON p.player_id = f.player_id GROUP BY p.bats), totals AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM fielders) SELECT f.bats, f.cnt, f.cnt * 1.0 / t.total AS share, f.cnt - t.avg_cnt AS above_avg FROM fielders f CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE f.cnt > t.avg_cnt;

assumptions.assumption: Each player's batting hand is taken from the player table, and fielding rows whose player_id has no matching player row are dropped by the inner join. GROUP BY p.bats keeps NULL and blank values as their own groups.

The total is the sum of the per-hand distinct-player counts, and the average is the mean of those per-hand counts across all hand groups, including blank and NULL groups. Since each player has one bats value, the total equals the number of distinct fielding players.
